subject: VectorLabs renewal: tiered capacity uplift and conditional price-hold proposal
messages:
From: Ari Goldstein <agoldstein@vectorlabs.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + ask: uplift and price-hold option

Ben —

Quick context: our renewal with Redwood comes up in July. Over the past 9 months we’ve steadily increased inference volume and are forecasting a 30–40% uplift for H2 if we proceed with the next product launch.

Two asks to kick off the conversation:
- Can Redwood offer a conditional price-hold (flat per-token rate) for 12 months if we commit to an increased monthly minimum (we're looking at a 20%–30% uplift in committed tokens)?
- If a price-hold isn’t feasible at full uplift, are there short-term credits (one-time) or a phased discount ladder you’d consider to smooth the transition?

I attached our current usage export (VL-usage-runbook.xlsx) to make numbers easy. Also looping in Maya (platform lead) and procurement for timelines.

Goal: get a commercial proposal this week so legal can review an amendment. Our budget window closes mid-May.

Thanks —
Ari
Ari Goldstein
Head of Platform, VectorLabs
agoldstein@vectorlabs.com

Attachment: VL-usage-runbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ari Goldstein <agoldstein@vectorlabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + ask: uplift and price-hold option

Ari —

Appreciate the data and timeline. We can absolutely structure something that reduces volatility during your launch. High-level options we can put on the table immediately:

1) Tiered uplift + conditional 12-month price-hold
   - If VectorLabs increases committed monthly tokens by >=20% we can lock the current hosted per-token rate for 12 months.
   - For >=30% commit uplift we can offer an additional 8% discount on top of the locked rate.

2) Phased credit + temporary discount (if you prefer ramp protection)
   - One-time migration credit applied over first 3 invoice cycles (amount configurable; suggest $30k or token-equivalent).
   - 6-month graduated discount ladder (3% -> 6% -> 8%) to soften initial spikes.

3) Dedicated capacity conversation (if deterministic latency/cSLA needed)
   - If you want to move to Dedicated pool for guaranteed throughput, we can model Reserved capacity pricing and provide a separate amendment.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm which option you prefer (Tiered price-hold vs phased credits).
- Send target uplift % (20%/30%/40%) and milestone dates.
- We’ll prepare a commercial term sheet + amendment draft for legal by May 11.

I attached a short proposal doc; Laura and Neha are cc’d to help size the credit and finalize pricing.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-proposal-v2.pdf (summary of options)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: VectorLabs concession plan and recommended structure

Laura / Neha —

Notes from my convo with Ari. He wants price stability during a sizable expected volume increase. Procurement is tight on mid-May. Suggested internal concessions and rationale below — please treat as internal until we publish the amended term sheet.

Recommended commercial posture:
- Base ask: 12-month price-hold tied to commit uplift >=20%. This preserves revenue predictability.
- Escalator: 8% additional discount if commit >=30% (gives a target for larger deal).
- One-time credit: $25k applied across first 2 invoices if they sign amendment by May 18 (motivates quick close).
- If VectorLabs wants 15-month hold, counter with a higher commit (>=40%) and require a minimum annual spend floor.

Margin / ops considerations:
- We can absorb short-term variance via caching/batching optimizations; recommend enabling prefix caching and suggest they adopt our long-sequence quant profile to reduce per-token compute. Neha: confirm that a 8% discount at 30% uplift is sustainable from a cost perspective.

Ask: Neha — run model tonight showing net margin at current usage, +20%, +30%, +40% for the two price-hold scenarios + credit. Laura — prepare amendment skeleton and legal-friendly language for the credit and hold clauses.

Thanks,
Ben

(Internal attachment: VL-deal-sizing.xlsx)
From: Ari Goldstein <agoldstein@vectorlabs.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Chen <mchen@vectorlabs.com>, Procurement Team <procure@vectorlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + ask: uplift and price-hold option

Ben / team —

Thanks for the quick outline — that’s helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement and platform:

- VectorLabs preference is a 15-month price-hold if we commit to ~20% uplift; we can stretch to 30% if the price-hold length is shorter (12 months).
- The one-time credit is attractive; procurement is pushing for $40k tied to an early-sign incentive (sign by May 18).
- Legal will want explicit fallback language that rates can be revisited if usage patterns materially exceed forecast (e.g., sustained >50% over forecast for 3 months).

Can you provide a redline-ready amendment and a final commercial sheet that shows exact committed monthly token targets for the 20%/30% uplift tiers? We’ll prioritize review if docs arrive before May 11.

Appreciate it —
Ari

Attachment: none
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ari Goldstein <agoldstein@vectorlabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procure@vectorlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: VectorLabs renewal: revised commercial and amendment draft

Ari / Maya / Procurement —

Attached: redwood-proposal-v3.pdf (final commercial table) and signed-amendment-draft.docx (redline-ready). Summary of what’s changed based on your ask: 

- Offer A (20% uplift): 15-month price-hold at current hosted rate; committed monthly minimum = (current avg * 1.20).
- Offer B (30% uplift): 12-month price-hold at current hosted rate minus 8% discount; committed monthly minimum = (current avg * 1.30).
- Early-sign incentive: $35,000 credit if amendment executed by May 18 (midpoint of your request and our internal axis).
- Fallback clause: explicit review if sustained usage >50% above forecast for 3 consecutive months; review aims to avoid unintended capacity strain.

Next steps:
1) If Offer A or B works, confirm which and we’ll send a DocuSign link for signature.
2) Legal redline and turnaround: Laura will manage comments directly in the draft.
3) Ops runbook: Neha will send an implementation checklist for prefix caching and billing alignment after signature.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8342 (updated).

Thanks for moving quickly on the timeline. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk the tables.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-proposal-v3.pdf, signed-amendment-draft.docx
